mitigation_mechanism: Domestic rooftop cisterns in semi-arid Brazil store rainwater for the dry period, giving households basic drinking and cooking water near the home, cutting the time spent fetching water and postponing or avoiding the extreme shortages that used to send families to water trucks [ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_1, ev_water_access_deficit_silva09_1, ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_4]. In a survey of beneficiary families, 57.8% said the cistern fully met drinking, cooking and personal hygiene needs [ev_water_access_deficit_silva09_2].
caveats: The benefit is set by storage per person: a 16 thousand-litre cistern gives a family of four 16.6 litres per person-day, and households of more than five people stay dependent on water trucks [ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_2, ev_water_access_deficit_brito07_1]. Only 19.1% of surveyed families named the cistern as their main water source, the survey used recall with no control group and was commissioned by the programme funder, and the other units are implementer or author statements [ev_water_access_deficit_silva09_2, ev_water_access_deficit_silva09_1, ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_1]. The evidence covers domestic water access as a component proxy for drought impact, not crop or livestock losses, and comes only from semi-arid Brazil.

justification.mechanism: Domestic rooftop cisterns in semi-arid Brazil store rainwater for the dry period, giving households basic drinking and cooking water near the home, cutting the time spent fetching water and postponing or avoiding the extreme shortages that used to send families to water trucks [ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_1, ev_water_access_deficit_silva09_1, ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_4]. In a survey of beneficiary families, 57.8% said the cistern fully met drinking, cooking and personal hygiene needs [ev_water_access_deficit_silva09_2].
justification.conditionality: The benefit is set by storage per person: a 16 thousand-litre cistern gives a family of four 16.6 litres per person-day, and households of more than five people stay dependent on water trucks [ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_2, ev_water_access_deficit_brito07_1]. Only 19.1% of surveyed families named the cistern as their main water source, the survey used recall with no control group and was commissioned by the programme funder, and the other units are implementer or author statements [ev_water_access_deficit_silva09_2, ev_water_access_deficit_silva09_1, ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_1]. The evidence covers domestic water access as a component proxy for drought impact, not crop or livestock losses, and comes only from semi-arid Brazil.

mitigation_mechanism: Runoff-fed storage holds water into the dry season: Kenyan communities with a sand dam had water 2.5 months longer than those relying on the riverbed, subsurface dams in Brazil raised well levels that households used when other sources dried up, production cisterns kept livestock watered while household tanks were dry, and pond water applied as supplemental irrigation during in-season dry spells reduced farming risk [ev_water_access_deficit_ritc21_1, ev_water_access_deficit_cirilo03_1, ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_5, ev_drought_hazard_brito07_10]. A review of small reservoirs and a Loess Plateau evaluation of runoff cisterns also credit them with drought resilience and with mitigating the effects of frequent droughts [ev_drought_hazard_saru19_1, ev_drought_hazard_iegchn07_4].
caveats: Storage capacity limits the effect: at least 67% of 30 Kenyan sand dams could not supply even one household through the whole dry season, and 57% of assessed dams would provide four months of water for their reported users only if it were their sole source [ev_water_access_deficit_ritc21_3, ev_water_access_deficit_neuf17_1]. The Loess Plateau drought claim is a qualitative assertion, the reservoir finding is a vote count, and the Brazilian pond statement is an institutional self-assessment without data [ev_drought_hazard_iegchn07_4, ev_drought_hazard_saru19_1, ev_drought_hazard_brito07_10]. Sand dams and subsurface dams are filed in this family provisionally, pending a sub-practice decision.

mitigation_mechanism: Drought impairs these works mainly by exhausting storage or suppressing their benefits rather than by physical damage: subsurface dams in semi-arid Brazil tended to dry out in a rainless year and small ones do not withstand long droughts, and domestic cisterns run out in great multi-year droughts so households fall back on water trucks [ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_2, ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_3, ev_drought_hazard_arsky20_3]. In Tunisia, consecutive drought years limited soil-conservation benefits and cut the works established in Medenine to 15 against a target of 95 [ev_drought_hazard_iegtun13_1, ev_drought_hazard_iegtun13_2].
caveats: Only the Tunisian shortfall is an establishment-phase loss of works; the other units describe storage running dry or benefits shrinking, and none quantifies structural damage [ev_drought_hazard_iegtun13_2]. The Brazilian evidence comes from interviews and field observation, and the Tunisian evidence from an ex-post review of project completion data [ev_drought_hazard_arsky20_3, ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_3, ev_drought_hazard_iegtun13_1].

mitigation_mechanism: Intense runoff overwhelms or breaks structures: floods washed away scores of small dams in northern Ghana, 37.9% of boulder-faced log check dams in Ethiopia failed after a high-magnitude runoff event, check-dam failure releases stored sediment, and large floods could wash out traditional spate diversions in Yemen [ev_flood_damage_veno12_1, ev_check_dam_failure_fran21_2, ev_check_dam_failure_fran21_1, ev_flood_hazard_yem12_3]. On slopes, banquettes lack capacity for erosive rains and overflow, diversion channels fill with eroded soil and overflow in the heaviest storms, and torrential rain collapses terrace walls or carries small terraces away in mass movements [ev_flood_hazard_heusch95_2, ev_flood_hazard_roose94_2, ev_erosion_hazard_willem21_3, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_5].
caveats: Failure is tied to maintenance and design: rarely maintained diversion systems generally fail after 4 to 10 years, terrace collapse is linked to abandonment, and the Rwandan mass movement happened on steep terraces without trees [ev_flood_hazard_roose94_2, ev_erosion_hazard_willem21_3, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_5]. Several hazards are extreme-rainfall or landslide events mapped to flood, the sediment-release statement comes from a USA study, and the Yemen statement refers to diversions before project improvements [ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_5, ev_check_dam_failure_fran21_1, ev_flood_hazard_yem12_3].
